title: fix(update): require the system-service updater cleanup receipt
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two gaps in the managed system-service update handoff, both found in review on the abandoned `release/2026.9.7` branch (2dc8fb8e29a5, with lint/fixture follow-ups 64deeeb77c01, 26478a45f25a and 7aecd8624360) and never forwarded to main:

- **Premature settlement.** The Gateway replacement join (`joinSystemServiceUpdateHandoffs`) treated the detached update helper as settled whenever it closed with an exit code and no signal. The helper's own SIGTERM handler exits with code 143, so a helper interrupted mid-update counted as settled and replacement could proceed while its detached updater was still running.
- **Dueling installs.** When the same systemd unit exists in both user and system scope, `admitSystemdUpdate` only kept system-scope restrictions for `kind === "system"`, so the operator-restart restriction for the system unit was silently dropped.

## Summary

- The helper writes a completion receipt (`system-update-settled`) for system-service handoffs; `observeManagedServiceUpdateHandoffClose` marks the owner settled only with that receipt plus an unsignalled close.
- `admitSystemdUpdate` admits `dueling` installs under the same system-owner restriction; lifecycle discovery stays user-first.
- `docs/install/update-troubleshooting.md` explains the behavior.

## Evidence

- Both defects reproduced on unchanged main via the ported regressions (settlement-control, dueling cases in `update-command-system-service.test.ts`, single-flight unwritable install); after the fix 52 focused cases passed (9 Linux-only real-process skips on macOS).
- `pnpm check:changed`: production typecheck and preceding guards passed locally before a host-load interruption; remaining lanes are on this PR's CI.
- Autoreview (branch mode): scoped-clean, no actionable findings.
- Not proven here: Linux real-process settlement run, live system unit, published-driver upgrade.


## Maintainer decision

Peter accepted system-owner restrictions for matching user and system Gateway units (2026-09-28): dueling installs keep the system-scope operator-restart restriction, and that outcome is explicit in the troubleshooting docs. This matches ClawSweeper's recommended option.

## Linux real-process settlement evidence

The real-process settlement cases skip on macOS and run on Linux CI. PR CI run 36416004744 (shard checks-node-changed-compact-small-5-2) executed and passed `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-settlement.test.ts > requires physical helper settlement at the public replacement join` for SIGTERM (556 ms), success (195 ms) and failed (204 ms) helpers; `update-managed-service-handoff-settlement-control.test.ts` passed its receipt/close join matrix in the unit-fast shard.

## Test cost (single worker, local macOS)

- `update-managed-service-handoff-settlement-control.test.ts`: 7 passed, 56.7 s wall (mostly transform).
- `update-managed-service-handoff-settlement.test.ts`: 3 skipped on macOS (Linux-only), 5.8 s wall; about 1 s of test time on Linux CI.
- `update-managed-service-handoff-single-flight.test.ts`: 24 passed, 38.2 s wall.
- `update-managed-service-handoff-command.test.ts`: 20 passed, 24.1 s wall.
- `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-system-service.test.ts`: 6 skipped on macOS (Linux system-service cases), 34.8 s wall.

Published v2026.9.6 updater x candidate cell: blocked on current main by an unrelated update-lane regression (P5, #160446: Doctor plugin source capture inside the read-only SQLite snapshot makes Package Acceptance `published-upgrade-survivor` fail on main itself). Per the maintainer, this PR lands on green CI; the cell is run on main after #160446 lands (one Package Acceptance run covering #160135, #160164 and #160129), and the release Full Release Validation runs the same cell on the re-cut branch as the binding proof.
